policy_prompt_for_subgoal: Read the required number N of execution cycles from the goal each time: 'again' means 1, 'two times' means 2, and 'three times' means 3; use the stated count for other explicit repetition counts. Initialize or update memory from the currently shown interval before applying these rules. An episode starts with A: select the cube identified by target_anchor in the initial execution scene. Later, if the interval ends with the raised hand in a grasp posture, choose B, regardless of completed_cycles. In these recordings approximately 46% finger opening after closing at table height and raising is sufficient evidence of that posture; an explicit held-object label is not required, and a cube center still reported on the table does not override it. A recognized table-height release followed by a fully open retreat takes precedence over lingering held or airborne object reports. After updating completed_cycles for that release, choose A when completed_cycles < N and C when completed_cycles >= N. Thus a completed A leads to B; a completed B leads to another A only if more cycles remain, otherwise to C. For every A, point at the current visible center of the same cube identified by target_anchor, allowing small shifts after placement; use the release trajectory in the current interval to disambiguate nearby cubes. Do not point at the raised wrist or an airborne cube centroid as a table grasp location. B and C require no point. Emit only the exact menu label as the choice: A, B, or C in this menu, without its action description. Supply a separate [y, x] point only for A. If observations are ambiguous or do not fit a rule, prioritize B when the final hand posture provides evidence of retaining an object; otherwise choose C only if the required cycle count has been reached, and choose A at the best visible match to target_anchor if it has not. This fallback must not override a recognized release followed by fully open retreat, and a lingering held or airborne object report alone does not establish retention after that sequence. Never count demonstration cycles or internal pick-up retries toward N.

fields.name: target_anchor
fields.description: With empty memory, inspect the demonstration to identify the cube grasped when the fingers close at table height and the hand lifts. Track that same cube through the rest of the demonstration and locate it in the initial execution scene. Follow continuous motion through exchanges, using direction and trajectory continuity rather than assigning identity by nearest endpoint or retaining the original grasp location. Resolve each exchange sequentially using continuous trajectories, carrying the tracked cube's identity and resulting location into the next exchange. Two exchanges return the target only when they swap the same pair of locations; exchanges with different partners can move it to a third location. Store its initial execution visible center as [y, x]. Determine this center from the demonstration and initial execution scene currently shown, not from an episode lookup, the original demonstration center, or the recorded grasp point. At every later step copy the incoming anchor unchanged. e.g. [122, 119]

fields.name: completed_cycles
fields.description: With empty memory write 0, ignoring demonstration actions. Otherwise inspect the execution interval shown at this step. Increment the incoming count once if the interval shows the hand descending in a partially closed grasp posture to table height, opening there to release, and retreating to a raised fully open posture. The first visible sample may already be partway through the descent; a raised starting sample is not required. Opening may be sampled at approximately 88–99% before reaching full opening during retreat. This sequence is a completed put-down even if an object report still labels a cube held or airborne. Leave the count unchanged for an interval ending in the raised partially closed grasp posture, even if that pick-up interval contains unsuccessful closures, incidental lifts, releases, or retries. Do not increment for the command being chosen now. e.g. 1
